documents.title: Generative AI Policy (v1.0)
documents.summary: Version 1.0 university policy from CTS setting core requirements for lawful, ethical use of AI by faculty, staff, students and affiliates. Its rules mostly bind faculty and staff and cover compliance, attribution, output review, bias, security review, data ownership and IP. It says nothing about student coursework rules.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no ban and no per-course delegation; it says faculty and staff "who wish to use an AI System must" meet conditions (legal compliance, attribution, output review, security review), so use is permitted with conditions.

units.why: The opening frames the policy purpose as "core requirements for the ethical, lawful and responsible use of AI systems", an institution-level framework statement, so P56 and informs.

documents.title: Guidelines for AI Applications in Academic and Administrative Work (v1.0)
documents.summary: CTS guidelines for students, staff and faculty on AI applications. They name Microsoft Copilot as the supported tool, steer users away from other tools for institutional data, and set best practices for data protection, integrity, disclosure and verification. Violations go to the Acceptable Use Policy; review is annual.
documents.stance_why: It names Copilot as supported yet acknowledges others "may still use others AI applications for personal or exploratory purposes" with caution, citation and verification; AI is allowed with conditions, not banned and not delegated.

units.why: The purpose states the guidelines "promote ethical and effective use of AI in academic and operational contexts" for students, staff and faculty, an institution-level framework: P56.
